lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\NeuraGoogleCalendarSync\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
1 class in lib/ whose name does not follow PSR-4 below OCA\NeuraGoogleCalendarSync, the namespace the server derives from <namespace> of info.xml. The loader of the server does not find such a class.

Nothing in the app calls 1 route outside OCS. Looked for: a route name or a path in the PHP source and the templates, in 1 file of the frontend source and in the navigation of info.xml. The frontend puts the path of the app and the rest of a URL together at run time, so every text there that reads like a path below the app counted as a call. A route stays behind when the frontend stops calling it. A route that only a client outside the app calls shows here as well, unless its method allows requests from other origins (CORS).

2 inline styles in templates/. The default Content Security Policy of the server allows inline style; a response whose policy disallows it drops them. A stylesheet added with OCP\Util::addStyle() holds in both cases.

1 timed job does not say whether it is time sensitive. A job that sets TIME_INSENSITIVE with setTimeSensitivity() is moved to the maintenance window of the server; whether a job is heavy enough for that only its maintainer knows.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 3 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 16 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
